Act as an ontology engineer. Use the following content (examples, part of the ontology, and a list of guidelines) as a guide to translate the natural language rule you are given into a SWRL rule. 
  EXAMPLES
    Example 1
    Rule in natural language: If a person has a sibling who is a man, then the person has a brother.
    SWRL rule: Person(?p) ^ hasSibling(?p, ?s) ^ Person(?s) ^ IsMan(?s, true) -> hasBrother(?p, ?s)

    Example 2
    Rule in natural language: if a person has a phone number that starts with '+', then the person has an international phone number.
    SWRL rule: Person(?p) ^ hasPhoneNumber(?p, ?number) ^ swrlb:startsWith(?number, "+") -> hasInternationalPhoneNumber(?p, true)

    Example 3
    Rule in natural language:  if a person has age greater than 17, then the person is an adult and has id card.
    SWRL rule: Person(?p) ^ hasAge(?p, ?age) ^ Age(?age) ^ swrlb:greaterThan(?age, 17) ^ IdCard(?id) -> Adult(?p) ^ hasIdCard(?p, ?id)

    Example 4
    Rule in natural language: if a publication has two different authors, then those authors have cooperated with each other.
    SWRL rule: Publication(?p) ^ Author(?y) ^ Author(?z) ^ hasAuthor(?p, ?y) ^ hasAuthor(?p, ?z) ^ differentFrom(?y, ?z) -> cooperatedWith(?y, ?z)

    Example 5
    Rule in natural language: if a researcher has published more than 10 papers in a Top-Tier conference, then the researcher is a prominent researcher and has a high citation impact.
    SWRL rule: Researcher(?r) ^ hasPublished(?r, ?c) ^ Conference(?c) ^ topTierConference(?c) ^ swrlb:greaterThan(count(?c), 10) -> ProminentResearcher(?r) ^ hasHighCitationImpact(?r, true)
  END OF EXAMPLES
  PART OF ONTOLOGY 
    ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:detectsIncident

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "detects incident",
        skos:definition "Indicates which incidents were detected by a specific detection activity.",
        skos:example "A flooding incident, a blocked road etc."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Detection
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Incident
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:incidentDetectedBy
    
    
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:detectsParticipant

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "detects participant",
        skos:definition "Indicates which participants were detected by a specific detection activity.",
        skos:example "Humans in danger, submerged cars etc."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Detection
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:VulnerableObject
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:participantDetectedBy
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:involvedInIncident

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "involved in incident",
        skos:definition "Indicates the incident a vulnerable object is involved in."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:VulnerableObject
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Incident
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:involvesParticipant
    
    
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:involvesIncident

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "involves incident",
        skos:definition "Certain analysis components recognize the major incident (e.g. fire, flood, etc.) portrayed in a media item."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Dataset
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Incident
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:involvedInDataset
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:incidentDetectedBy

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "incident detected by",
        skos:definition "Indicates the detection activity that detected this incident."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Incident
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Detection
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:detectsIncident
    
    
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:involvedInDataset

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "involved in dataset",
        skos:definition "Indicates the dataset this incident is involved in."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Incident
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Dataset
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:involvesIncident
DataProperty: beAWARE_ontology:hasDetectionConfidence

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "has detection confidence",
        skos:definition "Represents the confidence score of a particular detection.",
        skos:example "An image analysis algorithm detects a trapped car in the flood with 80% confidence."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Detection
    
    Range: 
        xsd:float
    
    
DataProperty: beAWARE_ontology:hasDetectionEnd

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "has detection end",
        skos:definition "Indicates the end of the detection."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Detection
    
    Range: 
        xsd:dateTime
    
    
DataProperty: beAWARE_ontology:hasDetectionRisk

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "has detection risk",
        skos:definition "Indicates the risk level of the detection."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Detection
    
    Range: 
        xsd:float
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:causedByIncident

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "caused by incident",
        skos:definition "Indicates which incident type has caused this impact type."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:ImpactType
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:IncidentType
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:causesIncidentImpact
    
    
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:causesDisasterImpact

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "causes disaster impact",
        skos:definition "Indicates which impact type is caused by this natural disaster type."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:NaturalDisasterType
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:ImpactType
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:causedByDisaster
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:isImpactOfIncident

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "is impact of incident",
        skos:definition "Links an impact to an incident."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Impact
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Incident
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:hasIncidentImpact
    
    
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:isImpactedBy

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "is impacted by",
        skos:definition "Links an affected object to an impact."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:VulnerableObject
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:Impact
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:hasImpactOn
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:causesIncidentImpact

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "causes incident impact",
        skos:definition "Indicates which impact type is caused by this type of incident."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:IncidentType
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:ImpactType
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:causedByIncident
    
    
ObjectProperty: beAWARE_ontology:characterizedByParameterType

    Annotations: 
        rdfs:label "characterized by parameter type",
        skos:definition "Associates a natural disaster type with a climate parameter type."
    
    Domain: 
        beAWARE_ontology:NaturalDisasterType
    
    Range: 
        beAWARE_ontology:ClimateParameterType
    
    InverseOf: 
        beAWARE_ontology:characterizesDisasterType
  END OF ONTOLOGY
  
  COMMON GUIDELINES

  Please try to implement the following guidelines:
  1: Variables e.g., (?something) used in Conclusions must be present in Conditions. So create as many variables as needed in Conditions. 
  2: Each atom must have exactly one variable if it represents class.
  3: Each atom must have exactly two variables if it represents object property.
  4: Each concept must be represented by a class and must be present in Conditions.

  END OF COMMON GUIDELINES

  The rule in natural language is the following: If an incident is detected and the confidence of this detection is greater than 0.9 and vulnerable objects are also detected, then the priority of the incident is set to 'high' and the detected vulnerable objects are involved in this incident.
  Give only the final SWRL rule

Using the provided examples, ontology, and guidelines, the SWRL rule for the given natural language rule would be:

```swrl
Incident(?i) ^ beAWARE_ontology:detectsIncident(?d, ?i) ^ swrlb:greaterThan(beAWARE_ontology:hasDetectionConfidence(?d), 0.9) ^ VulnerableObject(?v) ^ beAWARE_ontology:detectsParticipant(?d, ?v) ->
    beAWARE_ontology:hasIncidentPriority(?i, 'high') ^ beAWARE_ontology:involvedInIncident(?v, ?i)
```

This rule states that if an incident (?i) is detected (beAWARE_ontology:detectsIncident), the detection's confidence is greater than 0.9 (swrlb:greaterThan), and vulnerable objects (VulnerableObject) are also detected (beAWARE_ontology:detectsParticipant), then the incident's priority is set to 'high' (beAWARE_ontology:hasIncidentPriority) and the detected vulnerable objects are involved in this incident (beAWARE_ontology:involvedInIncident).
